tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

schema.name: ScheduleWakeup
schema.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

content.content:
# T-067 Three tiers: full art, the shape ronin, greybox

**Block:** session 5, polish · **Status:** done

## Goal

The author, Sun 15 Nov 02:40 (grill answers): the fall from the full version to medium and then to greybox should
read better. Full: the 3D hero with the rich effects; after the first cut the hero goes back to the model of before
the 3D models (the shape ronin) with today's effects; after the second cut the grey world with bare effects. His
warnings stay readable in every tier. (Plan step 3.)

## Decision

- **A sixth layer, the full art** (`FJamLayers::bArt`, `[JamLayers] ArtLostAt=1`): the 3D hero, his afterimages and
  (T-069) the rich effects. Losing it is a visible step down, so it counts in `Total`. The plain effects now go at
  the second cut with the materials (`EffectsLostAt=2`), so the medium tier keeps the glow, the sweep and the trail.
- **The shape ronin is back** as the middle look, as it was before T-061: body, head, hat, blade, its bob, lean and
  arm swing, its T-pose. It lives in `JamFighterRonin.cpp` (the view had grown past 600 lines).
- The road of cuts: 0 the 3D hero; 1 the coloured shape ronin; 2 the grey world, the grey ronin, bare effects;
  3 the T-pose; 4 the bean, the HUD gone. The stun and the win give everything back.

## Test seam

`Jam.Layers.TheArtGoesWithTheFirstCut` (red first; the two ini tests also went red until the line was added). The
test helper `OneLayerPerCut` now loses the art with its first cut, so one existing expectation changed: three cuts
take four layers, not three (the author's new tier, not a bent test). Checked in game: every tier, `-JamDemoSkipEvery=8`.
# T-027 The neon arena and VFX on stand-ins

**Block:** F · **Status:** done on stand-ins (real models and VFX wait for the art, T-025, T-026)

## Goal

The full look has to be worth losing: a neon arena that blooms, so the drop to the engine grid at the second cut
reads as a loss.

## Scope

- `M_JamNeon` (`/Game/Materials`): unlit, all emission, `Color` times `Glow`; made by
  `Tools/Editor/create_neon_material.py` (headless pythonscript commandlet). `JamShapes::Glow` paints with it.
- Arena: posts, floor lines and a new neon band along the edge glow; the lines pulse on every beat of the 120 BPM
  music. The second cut still puts the grid on everything and hides lines and the edge.
- Effects (blades, flashes, warnings, sparks, rings) and projectiles glow; memos stay paper (glow 1).
- `JamNeonRules` (`View`, pure), numbers in `[JamNeon]`: `LineGlow(MusicTime)` (a kick on each beat, an exponential
  fall, never below the base), `Bloom(Layers)` (the camera blooms with the effects layer; the first cut takes the
  bloom with the effects).

## Test seam

`Jam.Neon.LinesPulseOnTheBeat`, `Jam.Neon.BloomGoesWithTheEffects`, `Jam.Neon.IniIsComplete`. Red first: 3 failing
with stub rules; on the way green the beat test caught a rounding epsilon in the code that dimmed the beat.

## Done

142 `Jam.` tests green, 0 code check warnings. Clip `Clips/t027_neon_arena.mp4` (30 s, bot). After the clip the posts

# C++ standard of the jam project

Ported from the CastleFight and Diskworld standards before the jam start. It holds working conventions only: no
game design. A new rule is added here only by the author's decision.

## Style

- Epic C++ Coding Standard + `.clang-format` in the root: tabs, Allman, braces always, `ColumnLimit: 140`.
  `check_code.py` checks the format, never align by hand.
- Comments and commit messages in English only.
- A comment describes the behaviour that exists, not the intended one. Change the behaviour, fix the comment in the
  same commit.
- Epic prefixes: `b` for bool, `F/U/A/E/I` for types.

## Decomposition

- A decision (who is hit, how much damage, what a rule allows, when the run ends) lives in a pure
  `namespace <Feature>Rules` with no world and no actors: `Public/<System>/<Feature>Rules.h`, free functions with
  `JAMGAME_API`, and a header line `Tests: Jam.<Area>.*`.
- An actor, component or subsystem only glues: collects inputs, calls the rule, applies the result.
- A big class is split into `.cpp` files by responsibility with one shared `.h`.
- Soft thresholds: a `.cpp` over ~600 lines, a function over ~60, nesting over 3. Exceeding one is a signal, not a
  ban: split or justify.

## Systems and dependencies

- Folders `Public/<System>` and `Private/<System>`, plus `Tests`.
- **The simulation does not know about the presentation.** `Core` and `Sim` never include `View`, `UI` or `Audio`.
  The directions are forbidden in the `check_code.py` ratchet (`SIMULATION`, `PRESENTATION`): extend both lists when
  a new system folder appears.
- Balance numbers (prices, health, damage, timings) live in data, not in code.
- Randomness of the simulation comes from a seeded stream, not `FMath::Rand`, so a run can be replayed in a test.

## Logs

- No `LogTemp` in new code. Use the category of the system or `DEFINE_LOG_CATEGORY_STATIC` for a single file.
- Warning and Error only for a breakage or a wrong setup; state changes are `Verbose`, per-tick traces `VeryVerbose`.

## Tests

- Every new decision in `*Rules` gets a test `Jam.<Area>.<Case>` before the code (test first). Glue with the engine
  is checked in PIE, a test is optional.
- The number of `Jam.` tests only grows; a failing test means reverting the change, not bending the test to the code.
- A bug is fixed separately from a refactoring, test first.

## Blueprint seam

- A new Blueprint exposure is opened when needed, not "just in case".
- Logic is not duplicated between an EventGraph and C++: the decision is in C++, the Blueprint only calls.
- Renaming a `UCLASS`/`UPROPERTY`/`UFUNCTION` visible in Blueprints only with CoreRedirects.
- Deletions (C++, assets) only through a dry run with counts and the author's explicit yes.

## Done (end of a task with code)

1. `bash Tools/Build/build_and_test.sh --open` is green: build, `Jam.` tests without failures, checks. The agent
   closes the editor and runs the full build itself, without asking.
2. Every new `check_code.py` warning is fixed or justified in one line of the report.
3. New decisions are covered by `Jam.` tests, their number did not drop.
4. A git commit in English.

# Sunday afternoon: one combined task, run in parallel

The author played session-5n: "everything else is great". This prompt replaces `PROMPT_full_tier_look.md` and `PROMPT_aura_shuriken_locomotion.md` (do not run them separately).

## How to run it

You are the orchestrator. Split the work into tracks and hand each to a lead agent in its own git worktree, as many leads as you judge right (the tracks below are a suggestion, merge or split them). Each lead works test first in its worktree, then reports to you: what changed, tests, a screenshot or short clip of the look, open questions. You review every report against this prompt, send it back if it falls short, and land approved branches on main one at a time, running the full test suite after each landing.

The author approved the parallel run in advance: post a one-line forecast (number of agents, rough tokens, time) and start without waiting.

Constraints for the leads:
- The Unreal editor and the Unreal MCP are shared, and a build closes the editor. Agree slots: only one lead at a time works in the editor or builds. Binary assets (`.uasset`, Niagara systems, the level) cannot be merged: give each asset to exactly one track.
- Balance numbers live in `[JamBalance]` in `Config/DefaultGame.ini`; decisions in the pure `*Rules` with `Jam.*` tests, red first.
- Questions to the author go through you, as interactive questions, batched.
- We are past the 12:00 feature stop. Aim to land everything by about 17:00; whatever is not solid by then is left out and goes in the DEVLOG as not done. The final build must be stable: the video is recorded from it at 18:00.

## Track A: two quick fixes (land first, small)

1. The Ultimate charge aura says nothing while the meter fills. Bring back the Ultimate meter as its own bar under the hero's health, in every tier, as before T-072. The red aura under the hero shows only when the meter is full (and through the wind-up), never earlier. Shape ronin and greybox: the bar always, their ready cue only when full.

2. The hero's shurikens: 30% more per second, the same damage per second. Hero cooldown 0.4 s to about 0.31 s, damage per shuriken 9 to about 6.9 (round as the code allows, DPS within 2%). The hero only: the Publisher's stolen shuriken keeps exactly his current damage, spacing and speed. `ShurikenCooldown` and `ShurikenDamage` are shared with his stolen copy (scaled by `BossStolenCooldown`, `BossShurikenCooldownScale`, `BossStolenDamage`), so give him his own base keys or compensate his scales, and pin his current numbers with a test before the change. The hero's explosive shuriken (`ShurikenExplosiveEvery=3`) would explode 30% more often: ask the author whether to keep explosions per second the same (every 4th) or keep every 3rd.

## Track B: the full-art tier must be the most beautiful

The author: the hit effects still look like a lower tier (small flat sparks, red on the hero). The top tier should be as beautiful as we can make it so the fall to the lower tiers is felt. No hardware ray tracing (judges' GPUs may lack it).

1. Remove the flat greybox layer from the full-art tier. `AJamEffectsView::DrawBurst` (`Source/JamGame/Private/View/JamEffectsView.cpp`) still draws plain discs in every tier: hit, slam, explosion, deflect, heal. In the full-art tier Niagara alone shows these events; the discs stay in shape ronin and greybox. Keep anything that carries gameplay information (telegraph circles, the slam warning) unless a Niagara version replaces it clearly. The tier choice is a rule with a test.
2. Rework the T-069 Niagara systems (`/Game/FX/NS_JamHitSparks`, `NS_JamSlamDust`, `NS_JamCashBurst`, `NS_JamTrail`, `NS_JamEmbers`; built on two simple materials, then cut down, the trail never checked by eye): hits get a bright core flash with a short-lived point light, more and longer streaks; slams and blasts a shockwave ring; cash bursts sparkle. entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

Environment session here (megajam2026-bd): the author asked me to build a detailed arena (rooftop shrine) for the full-art tier, so I need to agree ownership and editor slots with you.
Plan: wet slate floor (PBRgen material + crest decal), 16 lantern-pillars replacing the posts, torii gates, stone lanterns, bonsai, a railing, a city backdrop, rain with puddle splashes under footsteps. All in the full-art tier; after the first cut a bare shrine (floor + pillars); the greybox stays as today. Work until about 21:00 UTC.
What I propose to own: AJamArenaView (Source/JamGame/*/View/JamArenaView.*), a new arena tier rule with Jam.* tests, new assets under /Game/Arena/ and /Game/FX/NS_JamRain*. I will not touch /Game/Maps/Arena or your Track B Niagara systems.
Questions: 1) Does Track B already add arena neon lights or edit JamArenaView / the level? If it does, tell me what, so we split it. 2) Editor and build slots: let me know when the editor and builds are free; I will ping you before every build or MCP editor session and work in a git worktree until then. 3) Your 17:00 landing / 18:00 video build: I will not land on main before your final build unless you say otherwise.

r5_boss_wide_apose {'width': 1024, 'height': 1536} high 
 Model sheet for image-to-3D: character concept art for a stylized 3D action game, ONE character, full body, strict front view, symmetrical, neutral WIDE A-pose: both arms held straight out and down at about 45 degrees, well away from the body, a clear gap of plain background between each arm and the belly and between the legs, EMPTY OPEN HANDS with fingers slightly apart, no weapons, nothing held. The Publisher, a satirical caricature of a greedy video game publisher as an angry indie developer would draw him: an enormous sumo-built executive with a gigantic round belly, an open cream white double-breasted suit jacket that cannot close, a black shirt with no belt, a plain thin shiny gold tie with NOTHING attached to it (no phone, no device, no chart, no clip), huge fists in gold plated knuckle guards. His eyes are glowing gold dollar signs, a smug toothy grin with one gold tooth, a shaved head with a tiny top knot, a gold dollar-sign lapel pin, a breast pocket stuffed with banknotes, red shirt cuffs, black shoes with gold trim. Comic, exaggerated, mocking but readable. Gold, cream white, deep black, a red accent. Stylized exaggerated proportions, big clean shapes, hand-painted game look in the spirit of Hades and Hi-Fi Rush. Flat even studio lighting, no cast shadows, plain light grey background, no text, no real logos, no floor shadow, the whole figure fits in the frame with margin. 

r5_cash_stack {'width': 1024, 'height': 1024} high 
 Model sheet for image-to-3D: game prop concept art, a single object alone, three-quarter view from slightly above, centred, the whole object fits in the frame with margin. A fat chunky stack of green paper banknotes, about forty bills thick, held by a wide shiny gold paper band around the middle with a big embossed dollar sign on the band, the edges of the bills slightly uneven. Stylized cartoon money, no real currency design, no portraits, no readable text or numbers. Green and gold, simple bold shapes, hand-painted game look in the spirit of Hades and Hi-Fi Rush. Flat even studio lighting, no cast shadows, plain light grey background. 

r5_dollar_card {'width': 1536, 'height': 640} high 
 Game texture: a single stylized cartoon banknote seen flat from straight above, perfectly rectangular, filling the whole frame edge to edge with no background visible, no perspective, no shadow. Light mint green paper with a darker green ornamental border, a big bold dollar sign in a central oval where a portrait would be, two small round seals at the sides, simple guilloche line patterns. Not a real currency: no portraits, no readable text, no numbers. Clean flat colours, hand-painted game look, readable when tiny. 

r5_memo_card {'width': 1024, 'height': 1440} high 
 Game texture: a single sheet of white office paper seen flat from straight above, perfectly rectangular, filling the whole frame edge to edge with no background visible, no perspective, no shadow. A corporate memo: a thick black header bar at the top, rows of grey scribbled illegible lines as text, a big red rubber-stamp rectangle at an angle in the lower half with blotchy ink and no letters in it, a faint brown coffee ring in a corner. No readable words, no numbers, no logos. Clean flat shapes, hand-painted game look, readable when tiny.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Autonomous build + automation test cycle for the jam project (ported from the CastleFight and Diskworld tooling).
#   build_and_test.sh [--no-build] [--no-test] [--no-check] [--open] [--filter Jam.]
# Closes this checkout's JamGame editor only (graceful first, forced after 30 s; editors of other worktrees and
# projects stay open),
# runs the full editor build, runs the project's automation tests headless and prints a summary, then the
# Tools pytest suite and the code checks (Tools/Quality/check_code.py, warnings only).
# --open relaunches the editor afterwards; ignored in a linked git worktree.
set -u
UE="F:/Program Files/Epic Games/UE_5.8"
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd -W)"
PROJ="$ROOT/JamGame.uproject"
LOGDIR="$ROOT/Saved/Logs"
OUT="$ROOT/Saved/BuildCycle"
mkdir -p "$OUT"

DO_BUILD=1; DO_TEST=1; DO_CHECK=1; DO_OPEN=0; FILTER="Jam."
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
	case "$1" in
		--no-build) DO_BUILD=0 ;;
		--no-test) DO_TEST=0 ;;
		--no-check) DO_CHECK=0 ;;
		--open) DO_OPEN=1 ;;
		--filter) shift; FILTER="$1" ;;
	esac
	shift
done

# A linked git worktree never opens an editor: there is one MCP port and the main
# checkout owns it.
# Both paths absolute: plain --git-dir is relative in the main checkout and absolute in a worktree.
if [ "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir 2>/dev/null)" != "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
	IS_WORKTREE=1
else
	IS_WORKTREE=0
fi

# PIDs of UnrealEditor processes opened on this checkout's JamGame.uproject. Matched by full path, so editors of
# other worktrees and of other projects stay open.
editor_pids() {

# Claude in Chrome

Claude in Chrome is a browser extension. Its tools, named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`, act in the person's real Chrome, in new tabs alongside the person's own, with their existing sign-ins. Claude in Chrome is available only while the person's Chrome is running with the extension connected; if its tool calls report that the extension is not connected or get no response, Claude says so rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

If the only Claude in Chrome tool present is `enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome`, Claude calls it first: it turns Claude in Chrome on for this conversation, and the `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools appear once it has run.

## Loading the tools

If the `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools are deferred (meaning they have to be loaded through ToolSearch before use), Claude loads every tool it expects to need in ONE ToolSearch call, because the select query accepts a comma-separated list and each extra ToolSearch call costs a full round trip. The core set to start with:

```
ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"
```

Claude adds task-specific tools to that same call when the task obviously needs them: `read_console_messages` and `read_network_requests` for debugging, `form_input` for forms, `gif_creator` for recordings, `javascript_tool` for page scripting. A second ToolSearch is only for a tool the task turned out to need later.

## Starting a session: tab context first, then a new tab

At the start of each browser session Claude calls `mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp` first, to see the person's current tabs and understand what they may want to work with. Then:

1. Claude reuses an existing tab only when the person explicitly asks to work with it.
2. Otherwise Claude opens a new tab with `mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp` and works there, and, unless the person wants them kept, closes the tabs it created before finishing.
3. Claude never reuses tab IDs remembered from an earlier or different session. If a tool reports that a tab does not exist or is invalid, or the person closes a tab, or a navigation error occurs, Claude calls `tabs_context_mcp` again for fresh tab IDs.

## Site permissions

Claude in Chrome acts on a site only once the person has allowed it; depending on their settings the person may be prompted per site, in the extension or in the app. When a tool call is waiting on or refused that permission, Claude tells the person and waits for them to allow it rather than working around it. A site the person declines is their decision; Claude moves on.

## Recording a GIF

For multi-step interactions the person may want to review or share, Claude can record them with `mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator`. Claude captures a few extra frames before and after each action so playback is smooth, and gives the file a meaningful name (for example "login_process.gif").

## Reading console output

`mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages` reads the page's console. Console output can be verbose, so when Claude is looking for specific entries it passes the `pattern` parameter (a regular expression), for example pattern "[MyApp]" to keep only the application's own logs.

## Alerts and dialogs

Claude does not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or other browser modal dialogs through its actions. Those dialogs block all further browser events, so the extension stops receiving commands. Instead:

1. Claude avoids clicking elements likely to raise a confirmation dialog (for example a "Delete" button) unless necessary.
2. If it must interact with such an element, Claude warns the person first that this may interrupt the session.
3. Claude can use `mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool` to check for and dismiss an existing dialog before proceeding, and prefers `console.log` plus `read_console_messages` over `alert` for debugging.

If a dialog does get triggered and the browser stops responding, Claude tells the person they need to dismiss it manually in Chrome.

## Staying on task, and when to stop

Claude stays focused on the specific task and does not wander into unrelated pages. Claude stops and asks the person how to proceed, explaining what it tried and what went wrong, when any of these happen:

- browser tool calls fail or return errors after 2 or 3 attempts
- the extension gives no response
- page elements do not respond to clicks or input, or pages do not load or time out
- the task turns out to involve unexpected complexity or tangents
- several approaches have not completed the task

Claude does not keep retrying the same failing action.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

content.content:
1	"""Imports the approved 3D models into the project. Runs inside the editor, headless:
2	
3	UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe JamGame.uproject -run=pythonscript -script="Tools/Editor/import_models.py"
4	
5	The hero (Art/Models/hero_fixed, exported by Tools/Art/hero_export.py), the Publisher (Art/Models/boss_fixed) and the
6	props. Both characters come as one mesh FBX in centimetres plus one FBX per clip; FBX goes through the classic
7	importer (its options are stable from a script), GLB through Interchange. An asset that exists is imported again
8	over itself, so the script can be run after every new export.
9	"""
10	import os
11	
12	import unreal
13	
14	ROOT = unreal.Paths.convert_relative_path_to_full(unreal.Paths.project_dir())
15	ART = os.path.join(ROOT, "Art")
16	
17	CHARACTERS = [
18	    {
19	        "folder": "/Game/Characters/Hero",
20	        "source": "Models/hero_fixed",
21	        "mesh": "SK_Hero",
22	        "prefix": "A_Hero_",
23	        "clips": ["Idle", "Walk", "Run", "Right_Hand_Sword_Slash", "Left_Slash", "Sword_Parry", "Hit_Reaction", "Dead",
24	                  "Roll_Dodge", "Throw_L"],
25	        # Clips whose travel is on root (hero_export.py, boss_fixed/README.md): the game keeps the fighter in place.
26	        "locked": ["Hit_Reaction", "Dead", "Roll_Dodge"],
27	    },
28	    {
29	        "folder": "/Game/Characters/Publisher",
30	        "source": "Models/boss_fixed",
31	        "mesh": "SK_Publisher",
32	        "prefix": "A_Publisher_",
33	        "clips": ["Idle", "Slow_Orc_Walk", "Heavy_Hammer_Swing", "Charged_Ground_Slam", "Kung_Fu_Punch", "Hit_Reaction",
34	                  "Knock_Down", "T_Pose"],
35	        "locked": ["Hit_Reaction", "Knock_Down", "Kung_Fu_Punch"],
36	    },
37	]
38	PROP_MODELS = [
39	    ("Models/katana/model_glb.glb", "Katana", "SM_Katana"),
40	    ("Models/shuriken/model_glb.glb", "Shuriken", "SM_Shuriken"),
41	    ("Models/cash_stack/model_glb.glb", "CashStack", "SM_CashStack"),
42	]
43	PROP_TEXTURES = [
44	    ("Concepts/r5_dollar_card.png", "T_DollarCard"),
45	    ("Concepts/r5_memo_card.png", "T_MemoCard"),
46	]
47	
48	
49	def log(text):
50	    unreal.log("import_models: " + text)
51	
52	
53	def run(task):
54	    unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().import_asset_tasks([task])
55	    return list(task.get_editor_property("imported_object_paths"))
56	
57	
58	def task_for(source, folder, name, options=None):
59	    task = unreal.AssetImportTask()
60	    task.set_editor_property("filename", os.path.join(ART, source))
61	    task.set_editor_property("destination_path", folder)
62	    task.set_editor_property("destination_name", name)
63	    task.set_editor_property("automated", True)
64	    task.set_editor_property("replace_existing", True)
65	    task.set_editor_property("save", True)
66	    if options:
67	        task.set_editor_property("options", options)
68	    return task
69	
70	
71	def fbx_options(skeleton=None):
72	    ui = unreal.FbxImportUI()
73	    ui.set_editor_property("automated_import_should_detect_type", False)
74	    ui.set_editor_property("mesh_type_to_import", unreal.FBXImportType.FBXIT_ANIMATION if skeleton else unreal.FBXImportType.FBXIT_SKELETAL_MESH)
75	    ui.set_editor_property("import_mesh", skeleton is None)
76	    ui.set_editor_property("import_as_skeletal", True)
77	    ui.set_editor_property("import_animations", skeleton is not None)
78	    ui.set_editor_property("import_materials", skeleton is None)
79	    ui.set_editor_property("import_textures", skeleton is None)
80	    ui.set_editor_property("create_physics_asset", False)
81	    if skeleton:
82	        ui.set_editor_property("skeleton", skeleton)
83	        anim = ui.get_editor_property("anim_sequence_import_data")
84	        anim.set_editor_property("animation_length", unreal.FBXAnimationLengthImportType.FBXALIT_EXPORTED_TIME)
85	        anim.set_editor_property("import_bone_tracks", True)
86	        anim.set_editor_property("remove_redundant_keys", False)
87	    mesh = ui.get_editor_property("skeletal_mesh_import_data")
88	    mesh.set_editor_property("normal_import_method", unreal.FBXNormalImportMethod.FBXNIM_IMPORT_NORMALS)
89	    return ui
90	
91	
92	def size_of(asset):
93	    bounds = asset.get_bounds()
94	    e = bounds.box_extent
95	    return "size (%.0f %.0f %.0f) cm" % (2 * e.x, 2 * e.y, 2 * e.z)
96	
97	
98	def import_character(c):
99	    folder = c["folder"]
100	    run(task_for("%s/%s.fbx" % (c["source"], c["mesh"]), folder, c["mesh"], fbx_options()))
101	    mesh = unreal.load_asset("%s/%s" % (folder, c["mesh"]))
102	    skeleton = mesh.get_editor_property("skeleton") if mesh else None
103	    if not skeleton:
104	        log("FAILED %s" % c["mesh"])
105	        return
106	    log("%s: %s, skeleton %s" % (c["mesh"], size_of(mesh), skeleton.get_name()))
107	    for clip in c["clips"]:
108	        name = c["prefix"] + clip
109	        run(task_for("%s/%s.fbx" % (c["source"], clip), folder + "/Anims", name, fbx_options(skeleton)))
110	        seq = unreal.load_asset("%s/Anims/%s" % (folder, name))
111	        if not isinstance(seq, unreal.AnimSequence):
112	            log("FAILED %s" % name)
113	            continue
114	        if clip in c["locked"]:
115	            seq.set_editor_property("force_root_lock", True)
116	            seq.set_editor_property("root_motion_root_lock", unreal.RootMotionRootLock.REF_POSE)
117	        log("%s: %.2f s, root lock %s" % (name, seq.get_play_length(), seq.get_editor_property("force_root_lock")))
118	
119	
120	def import_props():
121	    for source, folder, name in PROP_MODELS:
122	        run(task_for(source, "/Game/Props/" + folder, name))
123	        mesh = unreal.load_asset("/Game/Props/%s/%s" % (folder, name))
124	        log("%s: %s" % (name, size_of(mesh) if mesh else "FAILED"))
125	    for source, name in PROP_TEXTURES:
126	        log("%s: %s" % (name, run(task_for(source, "/Game/Props/Textures", name))))
127

"""Imports the approved 3D models into the project. Runs inside the editor, headless:

UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe JamGame.uproject -run=pythonscript -script="Tools/Editor/import_models.py"

The hero (Art/Models/hero_fixed, exported by Tools/Art/hero_export.py), the Publisher (Art/Models/boss_fixed) and the
props. Both characters come as one mesh FBX in centimetres plus one FBX per clip; FBX goes through the classic
importer (its options are stable from a script), GLB through Interchange. An asset that exists is imported again
over itself, so the script can be run after every new export.
"""
import os

import unreal

ROOT = unreal.Paths.convert_relative_path_to_full(unreal.Paths.project_dir())
ART = os.path.join(ROOT, "Art")

CHARACTERS = [
    {
        "folder": "/Game/Characters/Hero",
        "source": "Models/hero_fixed",
        "mesh": "SK_Hero",
        "prefix": "A_Hero_",
        "clips": ["Idle", "Walk", "Run", "Right_Hand_Sword_Slash", "Left_Slash", "Sword_Parry", "Hit_Reaction", "Dead",
                  "Roll_Dodge", "Throw_L"],
        # Clips whose travel is on root (hero_export.py, boss_fixed/README.md): the game keeps the fighter in place.
        "locked": ["Hit_Reaction", "Dead", "Roll_Dodge"],
    },
    {
        "folder": "/Game/Characters/Publisher",
        "source": "Models/boss_fixed",
        "mesh": "SK_Publisher",
        "prefix": "A_Publisher_",
        "clips": ["Idle", "Slow_Orc_Walk", "Heavy_Hammer_Swing", "Charged_Ground_Slam", "Kung_Fu_Punch", "Hit_Reaction",
                  "Knock_Down", "T_Pose"],
        "locked": ["Hit_Reaction", "Knock_Down", "Kung_Fu_Punch"],
    },
]
PROP_MODELS = [
    ("Models/katana/model_glb.glb", "Katana", "SM_Katana"),
    ("Models/shuriken/model_glb.glb", "Shuriken", "SM_Shuriken"),
    ("Models/cash_stack/model_glb.glb", "CashStack", "SM_CashStack"),
]
PROP_TEXTURES = [
    ("Concepts/r5_dollar_card.png", "T_DollarCard"),
    ("Concepts/r5_memo_card.png", "T_MemoCard"),
]


def log(text):
    unreal.log("import_models: " + text)


def run(task):
    unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().import_asset_tasks([task])
    return list(task.get_editor_property("imported_object_paths"))


def task_for(source, folder, name, options=None):
    task = unreal.AssetImportTask()
    task.set_editor_property("filename", os.path.join(ART, source))
    task.set_editor_property("destination_path", folder)
    task.set_editor_property("destination_name", name)
    task.set_editor_property("automated", True)
    task.set_editor_property("replace_existing", True)
    task.set_editor_property("save", True)
    if options:
        task.set_editor_property("options", options)
    return task


def fbx_options(skeleton=None):
    ui = unreal.FbxImportUI()
    ui.set_editor_property("automated_import_should_detect_type", False)
    ui.set_editor_property("mesh_type_to_import", unreal.FBXImportType.FBXIT_ANIMATION if skeleton else unreal.FBXImportType.FBXIT_SKELETAL_MESH)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_mesh", skeleton is None)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_as_skeletal", True)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_animations", skeleton is not None)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_materials", skeleton is None)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_textures", skeleton is None)
    ui.set_editor_property("create_physics_asset", False)
    if skeleton:
        ui.set_editor_property("skeleton", skeleton)
        anim = ui.get_editor_property("anim_sequence_import_data")
        anim.set_editor_property("animation_length", unreal.FBXAnimationLengthImportType.FBXALIT_EXPORTED_TIME)
        anim.set_editor_property("import_bone_tracks", True)
        anim.set_editor_property("remove_redundant_keys", False)
    mesh = ui.get_editor_property("skeletal_mesh_import_data")
    mesh.set_editor_property("normal_import_method", unreal.FBXNormalImportMethod.FBXNIM_IMPORT_NORMALS)
    return ui


def size_of(asset):
    bounds = asset.get_bounds()
    e = bounds.box_extent
    return "size (%.0f %.0f %.0f) cm" % (2 * e.x, 2 * e.y, 2 * e.z)


def import_character(c):
    folder = c["folder"]
    run(task_for("%s/%s.fbx" % (c["source"], c["mesh"]), folder, c["mesh"], fbx_options()))
    mesh = unreal.load_asset("%s/%s" % (folder, c["mesh"]))
    skeleton = mesh.get_editor_property("skeleton") if mesh else None
    if not skeleton:
        log("FAILED %s" % c["mesh"])
        return
    log("%s: %s, skeleton %s" % (c["mesh"], size_of(mesh), skeleton.get_name()))
    for clip in c["clips"]:
        name = c["prefix"] + clip
        run(task_for("%s/%s.fbx" % (c["source"], clip), folder + "/Anims", name, fbx_options(skeleton)))
        seq = unreal.load_asset("%s/Anims/%s" % (folder, name))
        if not isinstance(seq, unreal.AnimSequence):
            log("FAILED %s" % name)
            continue
        if clip in c["locked"]:
            seq.set_editor_property("force_root_lock", True)
            seq.set_editor_property("root_motion_root_lock", unreal.RootMotionRootLock.REF_POSE)
        log("%s: %.2f s, root lock %s" % (name, seq.get_play_length(), seq.get_editor_property("force_root_lock")))


def import_props():
    for source, folder, name in PROP_MODELS:
        run(task_for(source, "/Game/Props/" + folder, name))
        mesh = unreal.load_asset("/Game/Props/%s/%s" % (folder, name))
        log("%s: %s" % (name, size_of(mesh) if mesh else "FAILED"))
    for source, name in PROP_TEXTURES:
        log("%s: %s" % (name, run(task_for(source, "/Game/Props/Textures", name))))


unreal.SystemLibrary.execute_console_command(None, "Interchange.FeatureFlags.Import.FBX 0")
# JAM_IMPORT_ONLY=Hero (or Publisher, Props) limits the run to one part.
ONLY = os.environ.get("JAM_IMPORT_ONLY", "")
for character in CHARACTERS:
    if not ONLY or character["mesh"].endswith(ONLY):
        import_character(character)
if not ONLY or ONLY == "Props":
    import_props()
# The task saves only what it imported; the skeletons, materials and textures made on the way are saved here.
unreal.EditorLoadingAndSavingUtils.save_dirty_packages(True, True)
log("done")

"""Creates the material of the 3D characters (the game loads MI_Hero and MI_Publisher by path: the mesh slots set below
do not survive the save, checked Sun 15 Nov). Runs inside the editor, headless, after
import_models.py:

UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe JamGame.uproject -run=pythonscript -script="Tools/Editor/create_character_materials.py"

M_JamCharacter is the PBR look of the Meshy textures plus two things the game drives:
- Flash (0 to 1) turns the body white and bright for a hit, FlashColor times FlashGlow in emission;
- the neon: the saturated parts of the base colour (the hero's cyan and magenta piping) shine NeonGlow times.
Metallic and roughness come from any channel of their textures (the hero has them packed in one glTF image, the
Publisher in two grey ones): MetallicChannel and RoughnessChannel pick it.
The textures come from Art/Models/<x>_fixed/textures (Tools/Art/save_textures.py). Running it again rebuilds the
material and the instances.
"""
import os

import unreal

ROOT = unreal.Paths.convert_relative_path_to_full(unreal.Paths.project_dir())
FOLDER = "/Game/Characters/Materials"
MASTER = "M_JamCharacter"
CHARACTERS = [
    # name, textures folder, mesh, metallic channel, roughness channel, neon glow
    ("Hero", "Art/Models/hero_fixed/textures", "/Game/Characters/Hero/SK_Hero", (0, 0, 1), (0, 1, 0), 3.0),
    ("Publisher", "Art/Models/boss_fixed/textures", "/Game/Characters/Publisher/SK_Publisher", (1, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 0.0),
]
MAPS = ["base_color", "normal", "metallic", "roughness"]
# The scene is lit for the dark stand-ins (exposure locked at 1, JamCameraRig): the Meshy albedo is scaled down to match.
ALBEDO = 0.3
# The Publisher is hit all the time: a strong flash kept him white for whole seconds (Sun 15 Nov clip).
FLASH_GLOW = 0.4
# How far a full flash turns the base colour white: all the way blanked the cream-suited Publisher.
FLASH_MIX = 0.35

lib = unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary
tools = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools()


def log(text):
    unreal.log("create_character_materials: " + text)


def import_texture(path, folder, name):
    task = unreal.AssetImportTask()
    task.set_editor_property("filename", os.path.join(ROOT, path))
    task.set_editor_property("destination_path", folder)
    task.set_editor_property("destination_name", name)
    task.set_editor_property("automated", True)
    task.set_editor_property("replace_existing", True)
    task.set_editor_property("save", False)
    tools.import_asset_tasks([task])
    texture = unreal.load_asset("%s/%s" % (folder, name))
    if name.endswith("_normal"):
        texture.set_editor_property("compression_settings", unreal.TextureCompressionSettings.TC_NORMALMAP)
        texture.set_editor_property("srgb", False)
    elif not name.endswith("_base_color"):
        texture.set_editor_property("compression_settings", unreal.TextureCompressionSettings.TC_MASKS)
        texture.set_editor_property("srgb", False)
    return texture

                         scalar(mat, "FlashGlow", FLASH_GLOW, -800, -60), -600, -150)
    emissive = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionAdd, neon, flash_light, 100, -500)
    lib.connect_material_property(emissive, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_EMISSIVE_COLOR)
    lib.recompile_material(mat)
    unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(mat, False)
    return mat


def build_instance(master, name, textures, metallic_channel, rough_channel, neon):
    path = "%s/MI_%s" % (FOLDER, name)
    if unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_asset_exist(path):
        mi = unreal.load_asset(path)
    else:
        mi = tools.create_asset("MI_" + name, FOLDER, unreal.MaterialInstanceConstant, unreal.MaterialInstanceConstantFactoryNew())
    lib.set_material_instance_parent(mi, master)
    for param, key in (("BaseColor", "base_color"), ("Normal", "normal"), ("Metallic", "metallic"), ("Roughness", "roughness")):
        lib.set_material_instance_texture_parameter_value(mi, param, textures[key])
    lib.set_material_instance_vector_parameter_value(mi, "MetallicChannel", unreal.LinearColor(*metallic_channel, 0))
    lib.set_material_instance_vector_parameter_value(mi, "RoughnessChannel", unreal.LinearColor(*rough_channel, 0))
    lib.set_material_instance_scalar_parameter_value(mi, "NeonGlow", neon)
    lib.update_material_instance(mi)
    unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(mi, False)
    return mi


master = None
for name, source, mesh_path, metallic_channel, rough_channel, neon in CHARACTERS:
    textures = {m: import_texture("%s/%s.png" % (source, m), "/Game/Characters/%s/Textures" % name, "T_%s_%s" % (name, m)) for m in MAPS}
    if master is None:
        master = build_master(textures)
    mi = build_instance(master, name, textures, metallic_channel, rough_channel, neon)
    mesh = unreal.load_asset(mesh_path)
    slots = mesh.get_editor_property("materials")
    for slot in slots:
        slot.set_editor_property("material_interface", mi)
    mesh.set_editor_property("materials", slots)
    unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(mesh, False)
    log("%s: %d slot(s) wear %s" % (mesh_path, len(slots), mi.get_name()))


def build_ghost():
    """M_JamGhost (T-064): the hero's neon afterimages. Unlit and additive: Color times Glow times Fade, brightest at
    the rim (a Fresnel term), so a ghost reads as a glowing outline of the pose."""
    path = "%s/M_JamGhost" % FOLDER
    if unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_asset_exist(path):
        mat = unreal.load_asset(path)
        lib.delete_all_material_expressions(mat)
    else:
        mat = tools.create_asset("M_JamGhost", FOLDER, unreal.Material, unreal.MaterialFactoryNew())
    mat.set_editor_property("shading_model", unreal.MaterialShadingModel.MSM_UNLIT)
    mat.set_editor_property("blend_mode", unreal.BlendMode.BLEND_ADDITIVE)
