  lantern glass) in GlowColor. The lantern pillars get a cyan and a magenta instance.
- M_JamArenaFloor: the PBRgen slate (Art/Materials/slate) tiled in world space, wet (roughness scaled down, the low
  spots of the height map darker and glossy as puddles), with the engraved crest (r7_floor_crest) over the centre.
  CrestRadius is set by the game to the arena radius.
- M_JamArenaCity: the city far below (r7_city_backdrop), unlit.
Running it again rebuilds everything over itself.
"""
import os

import unreal

ROOT = unreal.Paths.convert_relative_path_to_full(unreal.Paths.project_dir())
FOLDER = "/Game/Arena"
PROPS = ["lantern_pillar", "torii", "stone_lantern", "bonsai", "railing"]
MAPS = ["base_color", "normal", "metallic", "roughness"]
# The scene is lit for the dark stand-ins (as M_JamCharacter): the Meshy albedo is scaled down to match.
ALBEDO = 0.35
# The lantern glass and paper: base colour above this luminance glows.
GLOW_FROM = 0.6
PILLAR_GLOWS = {"Cyan": (0.0, 0.8, 1.0), "Magenta": (1.0, 0.1, 0.6)}
STONE_LANTERN_GLOW = (1.0, 0.45, 0.12)
# PBRgen exports, Unreal preset: <name>_<map>.png in Art/Materials/slate (renamed on download).
SLATE = "Art/Materials/slate"
SLATE_MAPS = {"color": "T_Slate_Color", "normal": "T_Slate_Normal", "roughness": "T_Slate_Roughness", "height": "T_Slate_Height"}
# One slate tile repeat in world cm.
SLATE_TILE = 400.0

lib = unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary
tools = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools()


def log(text):
    unreal.log("create_arena_assets: " + text)


def import_file(path, folder, name, options=None):
    task = unreal.AssetImportTask()
    task.set_editor_property("filename", os.path.join(ROOT, path))
    task.set_editor_property("destination_path", folder)
    task.set_editor_property("destination_name", name)
    task.set_editor_property("automated", True)
    task.set_editor_property("replace_existing", True)
    task.set_editor_property("save", False)
    if options:
        task.set_editor_property("options", options)
    tools.import_asset_tasks([task])
    return unreal.load_asset("%s/%s" % (folder, name))


def import_texture(path, folder, name, data=False, normal=False):
    texture = import_file(path, folder, name)
    if normal:
        texture.set_editor_property("compression_settings", unreal.TextureCompressionSettings.TC_NORMALMAP)
        texture.set_editor_property("srgb", False)
    elif data:
        texture.set_editor_property("compression_settings", unreal.TextureCompressionSettings.TC_MASKS)
        texture.set_editor_property("srgb", False)
    return texture


def mesh_options():
    ui = unreal.FbxImportUI()
    ui.set_editor_property("automated_import_should_detect_type", False)
    ui.set_editor_property("mesh_type_to_import", unreal.FBXImportType.FBXIT_STATIC_MESH)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_mesh", True)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_as_skeletal", False)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_materials", False)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_textures", False)
    data = ui.get_editor_property("static_mesh_import_data")
    data.set_editor_property("combine_meshes", True)
    data.set_editor_property("auto_generate_collision", False)
    data.set_editor_property("normal_import_method", unreal.FBXNormalImportMethod.FBXNIM_IMPORT_NORMALS)
    return ui


def fresh_material(name, folder=FOLDER + "/Materials"):
    path = "%s/%s" % (folder, name)
    if unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_asset_exist(path):
        mat = unreal.load_asset(path)
        lib.delete_all_material_expressions(mat)
        return mat
    return tools.create_asset(name, folder, unreal.Material, unreal.MaterialFactoryNew())


def node(mat, cls, x, y):
    return lib.create_material_expression(mat, cls, x, y)


def scalar(mat, name, value, x, y):
    n = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionScalarParameter, x, y)
    n.set_editor_property("parameter_name", name)
    n.set_editor_property("default_value", value)
    return n


def vector(mat, name, value, x, y):
    n = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionVectorParameter, x, y)
    n.set_editor_property("parameter_name", name)
    n.set_editor_property("default_value", unreal.LinearColor(*value, 1.0))
    return n


def texture_param(mat, name, texture, x, y, sampler=None):
    n = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionTextureSampleParameter2D, x, y)
    n.set_editor_property("parameter_name", name)
    n.set_editor_property("texture", texture)
    if sampler is not None:
        n.set_editor_property("sampler_type", sampler)
    return n


def binary(mat, cls, a, b, x, y, a_out="", b_out=""):
    n = node(mat, cls, x, y)
    lib.connect_material_expressions(a, a_out, n, "A")
    lib.connect_material_expressions(b, b_out, n, "B")
    return n


def constant(mat, value, x, y):
    n = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionConstant, x, y)
    n.set_editor_property("r", value)
    return n


def build_prop_master(textures):
    mat = fresh_material("M_JamArenaProp")
    base = texture_param(mat, "BaseColor", textures["base_color"], -1200, -300)
    normal = texture_param(mat, "Normal", textures["normal"], -1200, 0, unreal.MaterialSamplerType.SAMPLERTYPE_NORMAL)
    metallic = texture_param(mat, "Metallic", textures["metallic"], -1200, 250, unreal.MaterialSamplerType.SAMPLERTYPE_MASKS)
    rough = texture_param(mat, "Roughness", textures["roughness"], -1200, 500, unreal.MaterialSamplerType.SAMPLERTYPE_MASKS)
    albedo = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply, base, scalar(mat, "Albedo", ALBEDO, -1000, -150), -700, -300, "RGB")
    lib.connect_material_property(albedo, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_BASE_COLOR)
    lib.connect_material_property(normal, "RGB", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_NORMAL)
    lib.connect_material_property(metallic, "R", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_METALLIC)
    # The rain: everything outside is a little wetter than Meshy painted it.
    wet = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply, rough, scalar(mat, "Wetness", 0.7, -1000, 650), -700, 500, "R")
    lib.connect_material_property(wet, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_ROUGHNESS)
    # Glow: the bright parts of the base colour (lantern glass and paper) shine in GlowColor.
    luma = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionDesaturation, -900, -500)
    lib.connect_material_expressions(base, "RGB", luma, "")
    smooth = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionSmoothStep, -700, -550)
    lib.connect_material_expressions(scalar(mat, "GlowFrom", GLOW_FROM, -900, -650), "", smooth, "Min")
    lib.connect_material_expressions(constant(mat, 0.95, -900, -720), "", smooth, "Max")
    lib.connect_material_expressions(luma, "", smooth, "Value")
    tint = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply, vector(mat, "GlowColor", (1.0, 1.0, 1.0), -700, -750),
                  scalar(mat, "Glow", 0.0, -700, -820), -500, -750)
    emissive = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply, smooth, tint, -300, -600)
    lib.connect_material_property(emissive, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_EMISSIVE_COLOR)
    lib.recompile_material(mat)
    unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(mat, False)
    return mat


def prop_instance(master, name, textures, glow=0.0, color=(1.0, 1.0, 1.0)):
    folder = FOLDER + "/Materials"
    path = "%s/%s" % (folder, name)
    if unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_asset_exist(path):
        mi = unreal.load_asset(path)
    else:
        mi = tools.create_asset(name, folder, unreal.MaterialInstanceConstant, unreal.MaterialInstanceConstantFactoryNew())
    lib.set_material_instance_parent(mi, master)
    for param, key in (("BaseColor", "base_color"), ("Normal", "normal"), ("Metallic", "metallic"), ("Roughness", "roughness")):
        lib.set_material_instance_texture_parameter_value(mi, param, textures[key])
    lib.set_material_instance_scalar_parameter_value(mi, "Glow", glow)
    lib.set_material_instance_vector_parameter_value(mi, "GlowColor", unreal.LinearColor(*color, 1.0))
    lib.update_material_instance(mi)
    unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(mi, False)
    return mi


def import_props():
    master = None
    for prop in PROPS:
        source = "Art/Models/arena_%s" % prop
        textures = {}
        for m in MAPS:
            textures[m] = import_texture("%s/texture_urls.0.%s.png" % (source, m), FOLDER + "/Props/Textures", "T_%s_%s" % (prop, m),
                                         data=m in ("metallic", "roughness"), normal=m == "normal")
        mesh = import_file("%s/model_urls.fbx.fbx" % source, FOLDER + "/Props", "SM_Arena_%s" % prop, mesh_options())
        if not mesh:
            log("FAILED SM_Arena_%s" % prop)
            continue
        if master is None:
            master = build_prop_master(textures)
        if prop == "lantern_pillar":
            mis = [prop_instance(master, "MI_Arena_%s_%s" % (prop, tint), textures, 4.0, color) for tint, color in PILLAR_GLOWS.items()]
            mi = mis[0]
        elif prop == "stone_lantern":
            mi = prop_instance(master, "MI_Arena_%s" % prop, textures, 3.0, STONE_LANTERN_GLOW)
        else:
            mi = prop_instance(master, "MI_Arena_%s" % prop, textures)
        mesh.set_material(0, mi)
        unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(mesh, False)
        e = mesh.get_bounds().box_extent
        log("SM_Arena_%s: size (%.0f %.0f %.0f), %d slot(s)" % (prop, 2 * e.x, 2 * e.y, 2 * e.z, len(mesh.get_editor_property("static_materials"))))


def world_uv(mat, size_param, x, y):
    """World XY divided by a size parameter: texture coordinates that tile the same on any mesh."""
    pos = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionWorldPosition, x - 400, y)
    mask = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionComponentMask, x - 200, y)
    mask.set_editor_property("r", True)
    mask.set_editor_property("g", True)
    lib.connect_material_expressions(pos, "", mask, "")
    return binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionDivide, mask, size_param, x, y)


def build_floor(crest):
    have_slate = all(os.path.exists(os.path.join(ROOT, SLATE, "%s.png" % key)) for key in SLATE_MAPS)
    mat = fresh_material("M_JamArenaFloor")
    if have_slate:
        tex = {key: import_texture("%s/%s.png" % (SLATE, key), FOLDER + "/Floor", name, data=key in ("roughness", "height"),
                                   normal=key == "normal") for key, name in SLATE_MAPS.items()}
    uv = world_uv(mat, scalar(mat, "TileSize", SLATE_TILE, -1800, 0), -1500, 0)
    # The crest: centred on the arena's middle, CrestRadius across half of it.
    crest_uv_scale = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply, scalar(mat, "CrestRadius", 1500.0, -1800, 600), constant(mat, 2.0, -1800, 680), -1600, 600)
    crest_uv = world_uv(mat, crest_uv_scale, -1400, 600)
    centred = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionAdd, crest_uv, constant(mat, 0.5, -1400, 700), -1200, 600)
    crest_tex = texture_param(mat, "Crest", crest, -1000, 600)
    lib.connect_material_expressions(centred, "", crest_tex, "UVs")
    if have_slate:
        color = texture_param(mat, "SlateColor", tex["color"], -1200, -400)
        normal = texture_param(mat, "SlateNormal", tex["normal"], -1200, -100, unreal.MaterialSamplerType.SAMPLERTYPE_NORMAL)
        rough = texture_param(mat, "SlateRoughness", tex["roughness"], -1200, 200, unreal.MaterialSamplerType.SAMPLERTYPE_MASKS)
        height = texture_param(mat, "SlateHeight", tex["height"], -1200, 400, unreal.MaterialSamplerType.SAMPLERTYPE_MASKS)
        for sampler in (color, normal, rough, height):
            lib.connect_material_expressions(uv, "", sampler, "UVs")
        base_rgb, rough_r = color, rough
    else:
        base_rgb = vector(mat, "SlateFallback", (0.03, 0.035, 0.05), -1200, -400)
        rough_r = constant(mat, 0.5, -1200, 200)
        normal = height = None
    # Puddles: the low spots of the height map (below PuddleLevel) turn dark and mirror-glossy.
    if height is not None:
        puddle = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionSmoothStep, -900, 400)
        lib.connect_material_expressions(scalar(mat, "PuddleLevel", 0.35, -1100, 500), "", puddle, "Min")
        lib.connect_material_expressions(constant(mat, 0.2, -1100, 560), "", puddle, "Max")
        lib.connect_material_expressions(height, "R", puddle, "Value")
    else:
        puddle = constant(mat, 0.0, -900, 400)
    # Stone: the colour scaled to the dark scene, the crest mixed in by its own brightness.
    stone = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply, base_rgb, scalar(mat, "Albedo", 0.45, -1000, -300), -800, -400, "RGB" if height is not None else "")
    crest_mix = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionLinearInterpolate, -600, -200)
    lib.connect_material_expressions(stone, "", crest_mix, "A")
    crest_scaled = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply, crest_tex, scalar(mat, "CrestAlbedo", 0.5, -800, 700), -800, 600, "RGB")
    lib.connect_material_expressions(crest_scaled, "", crest_mix, "B")
    crest_alpha = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply, crest_tex, scalar(mat, "CrestStrength", 0.8, -800, 800), -700, 750, "R")
    lib.connect_material_expressions(crest_alpha, "", crest_mix, "Alpha")
    dark = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply, crest_mix, constant(mat, 0.35, -500, -50), -400, -100)
    base = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionLinearInterpolate, -200, -300)
    lib.connect_material_expressions(crest_mix, "", base, "A")
    lib.connect_material_expressions(dark, "", base, "B")
    lib.connect_material_expressions(puddle, "", base, "Alpha")
    lib.connect_material_property(base, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_BASE_COLOR)
    wet = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply, rough_r, scalar(mat, "Wetness", 0.45, -1000, 250), -800, 200, "R" if height is not None else "")
    glossy = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionLinearInterpolate, -200, 200)
    lib.connect_material_expressions(wet, "", glossy, "A")
    lib.connect_material_expressions(constant(mat, 0.04, -400, 300), "", glossy, "B")
    lib.connect_material_expressions(puddle, "", glossy, "Alpha")
    lib.connect_material_property(glossy, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_ROUGHNESS)
    lib.connect_material_property(constant(mat, 0.6, -200, 400), "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_SPECULAR)
    if normal is not None:
        # Puddles are flat water: the stone's normal fades out in them.
        flat = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionConstant3Vector, -400, 0)
        flat.set_editor_property("constant", unreal.LinearColor(0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0))
        water = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionLinearInterpolate, -200, 0)
        lib.connect_material_expressions(normal, "RGB", water, "A")
        lib.connect_material_expressions(flat, "", water, "B")
        lib.connect_material_expressions(puddle, "", water, "Alpha")
        lib.connect_material_property(water, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_NORMAL)
    lib.recompile_material(mat)
    unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(mat, False)
    log("M_JamArenaFloor built, slate maps %s" % ("found" if have_slate else "MISSING (flat fallback)"))


def build_city(city):
    mat = fresh_material("M_JamArenaCity")
    mat.set_editor_property("shading_model", unreal.MaterialShadingModel.MSM_UNLIT)
    sample = texture_param(mat, "City", city, -600, 0)
    lit = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply, sample, scalar(mat, "Glow", 1.0, -600, 250), -300, 0, "RGB")
    lib.connect_material_property(lit, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_EMISSIVE_COLOR)
    lib.recompile_material(mat)
    unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(mat, False)


unreal.SystemLibrary.execute_console_command(None, "Interchange.FeatureFlags.Import.FBX 0")
ONLY = os.environ.get("JAM_IMPORT_ONLY", "")
if not ONLY or ONLY == "Props":
    import_props()
if not ONLY or ONLY == "Floor":
    crest_texture = import_texture("Art/Concepts/r7_floor_crest.png", FOLDER + "/Floor", "T_ArenaCrest")
    crest_texture.set_editor_property("address_x", unreal.TextureAddress.TA_CLAMP)
    crest_texture.set_editor_property("address_y", unreal.TextureAddress.TA_CLAMP)
    build_floor(crest_texture)
    build_city(import_texture("Art/Concepts/r7_city_backdrop.png", FOLDER + "/Floor", "T_ArenaCity"))
unreal.EditorLoadingAndSavingUtils.save_dirty_packages(True, True)
log("done")

    lib.connect_material_expressions(dark, "", base, "B")
    lib.connect_material_expressions(puddle, "", base, "Alpha")
    lib.connect_material_property(base, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_BASE_COLOR)
    wet = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply, rough_r, scalar(mat, "Wetness", 0.45, -1000, 250), -800, 200, "R" if height is not None else "")
    glossy = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionLinearInterpolate, -200, 200)
    lib.connect_material_expressions(wet, "", glossy, "A")
    lib.connect_material_expressions(constant(mat, 0.04, -400, 300), "", glossy, "B")
    lib.connect_material_expressions(puddle, "", glossy, "Alpha")
    lib.connect_material_property(glossy, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_ROUGHNESS)
    lib.connect_material_property(constant(mat, 0.6, -200, 400), "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_SPECULAR)
    if normal is not None:
        # Puddles are flat water: the stone's normal fades out in them.
        flat = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionConstant3Vector, -400, 0)
        flat.set_editor_property("constant", unreal.LinearColor(0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0))
        water = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionLinearInterpolate, -200, 0)

        lib.connect_material_expressions(puddle, "", water, "Alpha")
        lib.connect_material_property(water, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_NORMAL)
    lib.recompile_material(mat)

def build_city(city):
    mat = fresh_material("M_JamArenaCity")
    mat.set_editor_property("shading_model", unreal.MaterialShadingModel.MSM_UNLIT)
    sample = texture_param(mat, "City", city, -600, 0)
    lit = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply, sample, scalar(mat, "Glow", 1.0, -600, 250), -300, 0, "RGB")
    lib.connect_material_property(lit, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_EMISSIVE_COLOR)
    lib.recompile_material(mat)
    unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(mat, False)

# T-080 The rooftop shrine: the arena of the full art

**Block:** session 5, environment · **Status:** in progress

## Goal

The author, Sun 15 Nov 11:50: the arena is fine for the degraded tiers but not for the start of the game, when
nothing is cut yet. Build it in detail. Three concepts were made (`Art/Concepts/r6_arena_*`); the author chose A,
the rooftop shrine in a rainy neon city. Grill answers: props from Meshy, time box until about 21:00 UTC, the middle
tier is the bare shrine, rain with a wet floor and splashes where the fighters step.

## Decision

- **Three looks** (`JamArenaRules::LookFor`): the full art is the shrine (slate with the engraved crest, 16 lantern
  pillars, three torii, eight stone lanterns, four bonsai, a railing, the city far below, rain); the first cut leaves
  the bare shrine (slate and pillars); the second cut leaves the engine grid with plain posts, as before. The neon
  edge band stays in both shrine looks and now carries the beat of the music; the floor grid lines are gone.
- **No gate at -X:** the camera looks along +X, a gate on the near edge would hide the hero.
- **Splashes:** one per stride under each fighter (`JamArenaRules::StepSplashes`, hero 110 cm, Publisher 180 cm),
  shrine only; a jump longer than a dash in one frame (a retry) does not splash.
- **Assets** by `Tools/Editor/create_arena_assets.py` (headless): Meshy props on `M_JamArenaProp` (the bright parts
  of the base colour glow: lantern glass and paper), `M_JamArenaFloor` (PBRgen slate in world space, puddles in the
  low spots of the height map, the crest's bronze lines laid in), `M_JamArenaCity`. Loaded by path; a missing asset
  leaves its place empty. Lights and post process stay with Track B (`AJamLightView`).

## Test seam

`Jam.Arena.EachTierHasItsLook`, `Jam.Arena.OneSplashPerStride`, red first (stub rules: 2 failing), then green.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Records a clip of the game playing itself: the bot drives the hero on the top-down camera.
#   demo_clip.sh [seconds] [output.mp4] [camera]
# camera: ignored since T-018 (only the top-down camera is left), kept so older calls still work.
# Opens a game window for the length of the clip plus the start-up: warn the author first.
# Extra game switches go in JAM_DEMO_ARGS, e.g. JAM_DEMO_ARGS=-JamDemoHoldUltimate (the bot never presses E).
# The game saves every frame as a PNG at a fixed 30 fps (see Source/JamGame/Public/Game/JamDemo.h), ffmpeg joins them.
set -u
UE="F:/Program Files/Epic Games/UE_5.8"
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd -W)"
SECONDS_TO_RUN="${1:-26}"
OUT="${2:-$ROOT/Saved/Demo/demo_$(date +%m%d_%H%M).mp4}"
# A fresh folder per run: frames of an earlier run must never pad out a shorter one.
FRAMES="$ROOT/Saved/Demo/frames_$(date +%m%d_%H%M%S)"
LOG="$ROOT/Saved/Demo/demo.log"
CAMERA="${3:-}"
mkdir -p "$FRAMES" "$(dirname "$OUT")"

# Git Bash would turn /Game/... into a path under its own install folder.
MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL="*" "$UE/Engine/Binaries/Win64/UnrealEditor.exe" "$ROOT/JamGame.uproject" /Game/Maps/Arena -game -windowed \
	-resx=1280 -resy=720 -nosplash -unattended -JamDemo -JamCapture="$FRAMES" -JamDemoSeconds="$SECONDS_TO_RUN" -abslog="$LOG" \
	${CAMERA:+-JamDemoCamera="$CAMERA"} ${JAM_DEMO_ARGS:-}
echo "[demo] game exit $?"
grep -E "LogJam[A-Za-z]*: (Warning|Error)|Fatal error|Ensure condition failed" "$LOG" | cut -c1-200 | sort | uniq -c | head -12

echo "[demo] frames saved: $(ls "$FRAMES" | wc -l)"
COUNT=$((SECONDS_TO_RUN * 30))
ffmpeg -y -loglevel error -framerate 30 -i "$FRAMES/f_%05d.png" -frames:v "$COUNT" -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -crf 23 "$OUT"
echo "[demo] ffmpeg exit $?"
ls -la "$OUT"

- ToolsetRegistry.AgentSkillToolset: Provides tools for listing, reading, and creating/updating skills.
- AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset: Automation test discovery and execution toolset.

Wraps the IAutomationControllerManager API (the same backend the Session
Frontend uses) to let MCP clients list available tests, run them, and
retrieve results.

Typical workflow:
  1. DiscoverTests() once per session to initialize workers and load the test list.
  2. ListTests() to find tests by name or tag.
  3. RunTests() with the desired test names.
  4. GetTestStatus() / GetTestResults() to monitor and retrieve results.
  5. StopTests() to abort if needed.
- ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset: Tools for listing, inspecting, and editing Config Settings sections
- DataflowAgent.DataflowAgentToolset: Dataflow Agent Toolset - exposes Dataflow graph editing operations as AI agent tools.
- DataRegistryToolset.DataRegistryTools: Provides tools for querying and inspecting Data Registries.
- GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset: Provides tools for listing, activating, and deactivating Game Feature Plugins.
- EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset: Tools for querying and modifying Unreal Editor state: console variables, asset imaging,
actor and asset selection, viewport camera, content browser navigation, and Play-In-Editor
session control.
- EditorToolset.LogsToolset: Provides tools for reading the Unreal Engine output log and controlling
log category verbosity.
- LiveCodingToolset.LiveCodingToolset: Live Coding compile toolset.

Exposes an MCP tool that triggers a Live Coding compile from the running
editor and waits for the result, returning the compile status together with
any captured LogLiveCoding output and UBT compiler diagnostics.
- NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Info: Niagara Toolset for general Niagara information and guidance.

Provides:
- Enum value lookups
- General usage information

Call these functions when you need context about Niagara types.
- NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Component: Niagara Toolset for Niagara Component operations.

Use this toolset when working with:
- Niagara Components on actors
- Runtime Niagara system manipulation
- User variable overrides on component instances
- FX-related operations in levels or blueprints

This is the primary toolset for runtime Niagara operations.
- NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Blueprint: Niagara Toolset for Niagara and Blueprint integration.

Provides utilities for creating Blueprint wrappers around Niagara Systems,
making it easier to expose Niagara effects as reusable Blueprint actors.

Use this toolset when you need to create Blueprint-based FX actors from Niagara systems.
- NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System: Niagara Toolset for Niagara System operations.

Provides comprehensive access to Niagara System editing, including:
- System, emitter, and module creation and modification
- Schema discovery for understanding structure
- Topology and Summary inspection for viewing current configuration
- Data access for reading and writing properties
- Dependency rollups via GetSystemDependencies
- Dynamic-input chain traversal via GetDynamicInputChain

This is the primary toolset for working with Niagara Systems in the editor.
- NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Assets: Niagara Toolset for discovery of Niagara script assets.

Provides:
- GetAssetDiscoveryInfo: project-configured asset discovery groups
- FindNiagaraScripts: asset registry search filtered by usage, visibility, name, and module usage bitmask
- GetNiagaraScriptDigest: decoded asset-registry tags for a single script

All functions read from the asset registry without LoadObject. Pair with
NiagaraToolset_System.AddModule to drop discovered modules into a stack.

Note: FAssetData JSON serialization does not include the TagsAndValues map (it
is not a UPROPERTY), so callers wanting decoded metadata for a result row from
FindNiagaraScripts must round-trip through GetNiagaraScriptDigest.
- GASToolsets.GameplayCueToolset: Provides tools for inspecting, executing, and managing gameplay cues and their notify assets.
- GASToolsets.AttributeSetToolset: Provides tools for discovering AttributeSet classes and their gameplay attributes.
- GASToolsets.AbilitySystemInspectorToolset: Provides tools for inspecting the runtime state of an AbilitySystemComponent.
Each function takes a direct actor pointer and raises a script error if the
actor is null or has no AbilitySystemComponent.
- PluginToolset.PluginToolset: Tools for creating, editing, enabling, and querying Unreal plugins
- PhysicsToolsets.PhysicsAssetToolset: Provides tools for creating and managing Physics Assets.
- SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset: Playwright-style Slate UI automation toolset.

Exposes snapshot, screenshot, and interaction tools for driving the
Unreal Editor UI programmatically.  Registered via UToolsetRegistry
so the ModelContextProtocol plugin picks them up automatically.

A shallow root observer (depth 0) continuously tracks top-level
windows.  Before working with a specific window or panel, call
Observe() on it to get deep widget coverage, then Unobserve() when
done.  Observers walk their subtree every ~100ms, assigning refs to
newly appeared widgets and keeping the ref cache current.

Input simulation uses direct Slate event APIs (ProcessKeyCharEvent,
ProcessMouseButtonDownEvent, etc.) rather than the AutomationDriver,
because AutomationDriver's synchronous API deadlocks when called from
the game thread (which is where MCP tool calls execute).
- GameplayTagsToolset.GameplayTagsToolset: Provides tools for reading and managing gameplay tags in the project's GameplayTagsManager.
- SemanticSearchToolset.SemanticSearchToolset: Toolset exposing the SemanticSearch plugin's hybrid vector + BM25 asset search
to the AI Toolset Registry.
- WorldConditionsToolset.WorldConditionTools: Inspect WorldCondition (FWorldConditionQueryDefinition, FWorldConditionBase) structs.
- PCGToolset.PCGToolset: Toolset for building and modifying PCG graphs
- PCGToolset.PCGSpatialToolset: PCGSpatial Toolset
- UMGToolSet.UMGToolSet: UMG widget toolset for AI-driven widget creation and tree manipulation.

IMPORTANT WORKFLOW - for every widget and slot returned by this toolset:
  1. Call ObjectTools.list_properties(widget) to discover exact property names.
  2. Call ObjectTools.get_properties(widget, [...]) with those exact names.
  3. Call ObjectTools.set_properties(widget, {...}) with those exact names.
Property names vary per widget class and CANNOT be guessed - list_properties is required.
Skipping step 1 causes set_properties to silently fail or set wrong properties.

Returns UObject pointers - ToolsetRegistry serializes them as {"refPath": "..."} automatically.
Pass returned Widget, Slot, and Parent pointers directly to ObjectTools or back to this toolset.

    loading levels, placing and removing actors, controlling the level camera,

- editor_toolset.toolsets.skeletal_mesh.SkeletalMeshTools: Provides tools for inspecting and modifying skeletal mesh assets, including
    the mesh/materials, bone hierarchies, and sockets.
- editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools: Provides tools for inspecting and modifying static mesh assets.
- editor_toolset.toolsets.string_table.StringTableTools: Provides tools for creating and editing StringTable assets.

    script that glues them together with custom logic. The script's purpose is

- editor_toolset.toolsets.texture.TextureTools: Provides tools for working with Texture assets.

- animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig.ControlRigTools: Tools for creating and editing Control Rig assets, including hierarchy
    management, graph operations, and node/pin manipulation.
- animation_toolset.toolsets.sequencer.SequencerTools: Core tools for creating and editing Level Sequences in Sequencer. Use
    whenever working with Sequencer - covers sequence lifecycle (create, open,
    close), playback control (play, pause, scrub, speed, loop), sequence
    properties (display rate, frame ranges, marked frames, tick resolution),
    actor bindings (add actors, spawnables, cameras, find and manage bindings),
    tracks (add, find, remove any track type), sections (range, easing, blend
    type, completion mode), selection state, folder organization, sub-sequence
    navigation, event tracks, track filters, and sequence locking. For
    keyframing use SequencerKeyframingTools. For Control Rig use
    SequencerControlRigTools. For outliner inspection use
    SequencerOutlinerTools.
- animation_toolset.toolsets.keyframing.SequencerKeyframingTools: Tools for keyframing and animating properties on the Sequencer
    timeline. Use when adding, querying, or removing keyframes on channels,
    setting default values, evaluating channels at specific times, working
    with the Curve Editor, or managing channel selection. Covers float, bool,
    integer, and string key types with configurable interpolation.
- animation_toolset.toolsets.controlrig_sequencer.SequencerControlRigTools: Tools for animating with Control Rig inside Sequencer. Use when adding
    Control Rig tracks to bindings, getting or setting control values (bool,
    float, int, position, rotator, scale, euler transform, transform), keying
    controls, baking animation to Control Rig, managing layered rigs and
    priority, masking controls per section, space switching (world, parent,
    control, bone), tweening and blending between keys, snapping controls to
    actors, mirroring poses, zeroing transforms, or managing animation layers
    (add, delete, duplicate, reorder, merge, collapse).
- animation_toolset.toolsets.outliner.SequencerOutlinerTools: Tools for inspecting and managing the Sequencer outliner tree. Use when
    getting a snapshot of the outliner hierarchy, querying node children,
    managing outliner selection, expanding or collapsing nodes, or toggling
    node states like mute, solo, deactivate, lock, and pin. Also useful for
    test verification of Sequencer UI state.
- animation_toolset.toolsets.conditions.SequencerConditionTools: Tools for managing runtime conditions on Sequencer tracks, sections, and
    track rows. Use when setting up dynamic conditions that control whether
    tracks or sections evaluate at runtime based on platform, gameplay state,
    or custom logic. Supports MovieScenePlatformCondition,
    MovieSceneDirectorBlueprintCondition, and MovieSceneGroupCondition types.
- animation_toolset.toolsets.custom_bindings.SequencerCustomBindingTools: Tools for converting and managing custom binding types in Sequencer. Use
    when converting between possessable, spawnable, and custom/replaceable
    bindings, querying what custom binding type a binding uses, accessing
    custom binding objects for property inspection, or changing the actor
    template class on spawnables/replaceables.
- animation_toolset.toolsets.import_export.SequencerImportExportTools: Tools for importing and exporting animation data to and from Sequencer.

    importing FBX animation onto bindings or Control Rig tracks, exporting
    animation to AnimSequence assets, or linking AnimSequences for
    auto-updates.
- aimodule_toolset.toolsets.behavior_tree.BehaviorTreeTools: Inspect BehaviorTree (BT) assets.

PBRgen for Unreal Engine and UEFN

Unzip the whole download first.

UNREAL ENGINE 5
  1. Once per project: Edit > Plugins, enable "Python Editor Script Plugin",
     and restart the editor.
  2. Tools > Execute Python Script..., and pick import_pbrgen.py in this folder.
  3. The material is in Content/PBRgen/Dark_Slate_Flagstone: drag MI_Dark_Slate_Flagstone onto a mesh.
  The material instance has DisplacementAmount (in centimeters), DisplacementZero,
  NormalStrength, RoughnessMultiplier and Tiling.

DISPLACEMENT
  Needs Unreal 5.3 or later and a mesh with Nanite enabled or enough
  triangles. The starting amount assumes one tile is 1 meter.

UEFN, OR BUILDING THE MATERIAL BY HAND
  Import the T_ textures and set them up as follows:
    T_Dark_Slate_Flagstone_BC    Default, sRGB on      Base Color
    T_Dark_Slate_Flagstone_N     Normalmap, DirectX    Normal
    T_Dark_Slate_Flagstone_ORM   Masks, sRGB off       R Ambient Occlusion, G Roughness, B Metallic
    T_Dark_Slate_Flagstone_H     Grayscale, sRGB off   Displacement

Coat, sheen and other OpenPBR maps are not part of this export. Pick no
software in PBRgen to get every map, with a .mtlx and a .usda.
